chunks: Al-Sadiq عليه السلام said regarding the reason for the ghusl of the day of Jumu'ah:

Indeed, the Ansar used to work with their water-drawing camels and their property. So when the day of Jumu'ah came, they attended the mosque, and the people were harmed by the odors of their armpits and bodies. Thus the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله ordered them to perform ghusl, and by that the sunnah became established.

key_terms.الْأَنْصَارَ: the Helpers of Madinah who supported the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.الْمَسْجِدَ: the mosque where the community gathered
key_terms.رَسُولُ اللَّهِ: the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله
key_terms.يَوْمِ الْجُمُعَةِ: the day of Friday, the day of congregational worship

ai.seo_question: Why was the ghusl of Jumu'ah legislated in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the practical reason behind the ghusl of Jumu'ah: maintaining cleanliness and preventing harm to others in communal worship. It shows that the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله instituted this practice, and it became an established sunnah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.230 - Imam Jafar ibn Muhammad Al-Sadiq (as) said regarding the reason for the Jumu’ah (ritual bath):

'The Ansar (residents of Medina who supported the Prophet) used to work in their fields and with their livestock. When Jumu’ah came, they would attend the mosque, and the people were bothered by the odor from their armpits and bodies. So the Messenger of Allah (sw) ordered them to perform ghusl, and thus it became a Sunnah (established practice).'
